items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: And then Roland Hanna, he came in after Tommy Flanagan and played with me.

ctx.x: Oh, Elvin took Persip's place, I see.
And Tommy Flanagan. Oh, I had a good band Oh, I really did. And then Roland Hanna, he came in after Tommy Flanagan and played with me. And --
How was he in those days?

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Roland played with you for…it wasn’t just that one period. He stayed with you for a while. ... Yes, he played with me off and on.

ctx.x: Were people now asking you for a draw?

Yeah, in fact at Birdland I had Tommy Flanagan playing with me. And he calls me and he says, “I got a substitute coming in for tonight, his name is Roland Hanna.” I said, “Man I never heard of him.” He said, “Well, he’s a good player.” So I said, “Has he been around New York long?” He said, “No, I think he just came in from Washington or something.” When I went to club he was already there. He says, “Man, I’d like to get a draw.” I said, “Well I haven’t even heard you play, I don’t even know whether I’m going to…
